exam_guide_revision: Practical Python data-stack curriculum reviewed against current official NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, and Seaborn documentation on 2026-09-19.

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; retrieval questions and typed coding questions provide the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Interactive first-pass learning for Seaborn. Emphasizes plot selection, DataFrame variable roles, semantic mappings, and preparing/aggregating data before composing statistical visualizations.

modules.title: Choose statistical plots and semantic mappings

nodes.title: Choose Seaborn plots from variable roles

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Start with the analysis question and the column __________, then choose the plot family.

reveal.text: Start with the analysis question and the column types, then choose the plot family.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Numeric vs numeric → `scatterplot`; one numeric distribution → `histplot`; numeric distribution by category → `__________`.

reveal.text: Numeric vs numeric → `scatterplot`; one numeric distribution → `histplot`; numeric distribution by category → `boxplot`.

prompts.label: 👀 LOOK FOR
prompts.placeholder: Category counts → `countplot`; matrix values by color → `heatmap`; ordered trend → `__________`.

reveal.text: Category counts → `countplot`; matrix values by color → `heatmap`; ordered trend → `lineplot`.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `hue` maps a variable to color, `style` maps to marker/line style, and `size` maps to visual __________.

reveal.text: `hue` maps a variable to color, `style` maps to marker/line style, and `size` maps to visual size.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use a semantic mapping when x/y answer the main relationship but another variable should remain visually __________.

reveal.text: Use a semantic mapping when x/y answer the main relationship but another variable should remain visually distinguishable.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Do not encode too many variables at once: additional semantics can make a plot harder to __________.

reveal.text: Do not encode too many variables at once: additional semantics can make a plot harder to read.

modules.title: Build common relational, distribution, and categorical plots

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `scatterplot` shows individual x/y observations; `lineplot` emphasizes an ordered __________.

reveal.text: `scatterplot` shows individual x/y observations; `lineplot` emphasizes an ordered trend.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Age vs income → scatter; month vs revenue → __________.

reveal.text: Age vs income → scatter; month vs revenue → line.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Color a scatter by segment with `sns.scatterplot(..., __________="segment")`.

reveal.text: Color a scatter by segment with `sns.scatterplot(..., hue="segment")`.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `histplot` groups numeric observations into __________ and displays how many/frequent values fall in them.

reveal.text: `histplot` groups numeric observations into bins and displays how many/frequent values fall in them.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use it to inspect skew, multiple peaks, gaps, and the overall __________ of a numeric variable.

reveal.text: Use it to inspect skew, multiple peaks, gaps, and the overall shape of a numeric variable.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: `countplot` counts categorical levels; it is not a replacement for a histogram of __________ data.

reveal.text: `countplot` counts categorical levels; it is not a replacement for a histogram of continuous numeric data.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `boxplot` compares a numeric distribution across categories; `countplot` shows how many __________ belong to each category.

reveal.text: `boxplot` compares a numeric distribution across categories; `countplot` shows how many rows belong to each category.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Income by segment → boxplot; number of customers in each segment → __________.

reveal.text: Income by segment → boxplot; number of customers in each segment → countplot.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: A box plot summarizes distribution; it does not show every individual observation unless another layer is __________.

reveal.text: A box plot summarizes distribution; it does not show every individual observation unless another layer is added.

modules.title: Use heatmaps, figure-level functions, and composed visualizations

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `scatterplot`, `lineplot`, and `histplot` are Axes-level; `relplot`, `displot`, and `catplot` are __________-level.

reveal.text: `scatterplot`, `lineplot`, and `histplot` are Axes-level; `relplot`, `displot`, and `catplot` are figure-level.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use an Axes-level function when drawing into an existing Matplotlib subplot via `__________=`.

reveal.text: Use an Axes-level function when drawing into an existing Matplotlib subplot via `ax=`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Figure-level functions manage their own grid/figure, so they do not drop into an existing Axes layout in the same __________.

reveal.text: Figure-level functions manage their own grid/figure, so they do not drop into an existing Axes layout in the same way.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `heatmap` maps matrix cell values to __________.

reveal.text: `heatmap` maps matrix cell values to color.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: A common correlation workflow is `corr = df.corr(numeric_only=True)` then `sns.__________(corr, annot=True)`.

reveal.text: A common correlation workflow is `corr = df.corr(numeric_only=True)` then `sns.heatmap(corr, annot=True)`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: A correlation matrix should be built from appropriate numeric variables; arbitrary category codes can create __________ correlations.

reveal.text: A correlation matrix should be built from appropriate numeric variables; arbitrary category codes can create misleading correlations.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `pairplot` creates a matrix of pairwise plots for multiple __________ variables.

reveal.text: `pairplot` creates a matrix of pairwise plots for multiple numeric variables.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use it for exploratory overview when several numeric columns may relate to each other and a category can be mapped with __________.

reveal.text: Use it for exploratory overview when several numeric columns may relate to each other and a category can be mapped with hue.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Pair plots become visually expensive with many variables because the number of panels grows roughly with the __________ of variable count.

reveal.text: Pair plots become visually expensive with many variables because the number of panels grows roughly with the square of variable count.

nodes.title: Data preparation comes before the plot

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: A real plotting workflow often follows `inspect schema → clean/derive → aggregate if needed → choose plot → map x/y/semantics → __________`.

reveal.text: A real plotting workflow often follows `inspect schema → clean/derive → aggregate if needed → choose plot → map x/y/semantics → label/interpret`.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: If the question asks for monthly averages by region, compute the monthly-region __________ before plotting.

reveal.text: If the question asks for monthly averages by region, compute the monthly-region summary before plotting.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Do not let a plotting function hide an unclear analysis goal; first decide what each output point, line, bar, or box should __________.

reveal.text: Do not let a plotting function hide an unclear analysis goal; first decide what each output point, line, bar, or box should represent.
